title: Junta Escalates Airstrikes to Retake Rakhine-Magway Border Corridor from Arakan Army
detail: Heavy clashes broke out August 2-6, 2026 along the Arakan mountain range — near the besieged Nat Yay Kan hilltop base, Goteseeyoe village, and Kamyinkan outpost — as junta forces backed by fighter jets, Y-12 aircraft, drones, and Artillery Battalion No. 905 pushed to recapture territory controlling a Chinese gas-pipeline route from the Arakan Army and its allies. A two-hour coordinated air campaign hit the area on August 2.

media.caption: Junta escalates airstrikes and artillery to retake the Rakhine-Magway border corridor from the Arakan Army.

title: Junta Troops Shoot IDP Fishermen Near Sittwe-Rathedaung Border — One Killed
detail: Junta forces opened fire on three displaced fishermen near Nanthar Island, on the Sittwe-Rathedaung border in Rakhine State, on August 3, 2026, killing U Nyunt Chay (47), an IDP from Aung Taing village, and wounding two others (U A Poo Chay and U Maung Maung Tun). The shooting occurred as the Arakan Army's advance pushed to within roughly 2 km of Sittwe, the last major Rakhine State town in junta hands.

media.caption: Junta troops shoot displaced fishermen near Nanthar Island on the Sittwe-Rathedaung border.

title: Aung San Suu Kyi Meets ICRC Official — First Known Meeting with a Foreign Official in Years
detail: Detained former State Counsellor Aung San Suu Kyi (81) met ICRC Myanmar head of delegation Arnaude de Baecque at 9:30am on August 3, 2026 in Naypyidaw, in what is believed to be her first known meeting with a foreign official in years, following mounting international concern about her health and welfare. The visit followed standard ICRC detainee-visit protocol, with findings shared confidentially with authorities only; the regime released four photographs of the meeting.

media.caption: Aung San Suu Kyi meets an ICRC official in Naypyidaw — her first known meeting with a foreign official in years.
